title: The Gnostic John the Baptizer
author: G. R. S. Mead
description: The Gnostic John the Baptizer: Selections from the Mandaean John-Book by G. R. S. Mead (London: John M. Watkins, 1924). The Mandaeans of southern Iraq and Iran, the last surviving Gnostic community, revere John the Baptist as their great teacher and practise repeated baptism in flowing 'living water'. Mead translates, largely from Mark Lidzbarski's German edition of the Mandaean Book of John (Drashe d-Yahya), the passages concerning John: his miraculous birth, his teaching and baptisms in the Jordan, his dialogues with the 'Messiah' and the Jews, and his death and ascent to the world of light. Introductory chapters survey Mandaean origins, cosmology and the controversy over their relation to early Christianity and the Gospel of John, and the book closes with essays on John the Baptist in Christian and Josephan tradition. It is an accessible early English gateway to Mandaean literature.
